questions.question: Which best describes the primary task format in GSM8K?
questions.choice_A: Short, grade-school math word problems requiring a single numeric answer with step-by-step reasoning
questions.choice_B: Multiple-choice questions across STEM disciplines with four options
questions.choice_C: Formal theorem statements in Lean to be proved from axioms
questions.choice_D: Open-ended essay responses graded by human raters

questions.question: What distinguishes the MATH benchmark from GSM8K in terms of difficulty granularity?
questions.choice_A: MATH is limited to arithmetic, while GSM8K includes calculus and abstract algebra
questions.choice_B: MATH includes competition-style problems with tagged difficulty levels, spanning a wider range than GSM8K
questions.choice_C: MATH uses only multiple-choice answers, while GSM8K requires free-form solutions
questions.choice_D: MATH requires program synthesis; GSM8K requires natural language proofs

questions.question: In the context of CMATH as a benchmark, what is a key design consideration researchers discuss?
questions.choice_A: It evaluates large-scale image classification pipelines
questions.choice_B: It standardizes formal proof generation in Coq exclusively
questions.choice_C: It targets math problem solving in a non-English setting and includes difficulty gradations to mirror competition math
questions.choice_D: It focuses on conversational tutoring with human-in-the-loop grading only

questions.question: What is the primary goal of MMLU as an evaluation?
questions.choice_A: Measure a model’s ability to generate formal proofs from axioms
questions.choice_B: Assess broad knowledge and reasoning across many academic subjects using multiple-choice questions
questions.choice_C: Evaluate sample efficiency in reinforcement learning environments
questions.choice_D: Benchmark program synthesis from natural language intent using unit tests

questions.question: Which statement about BBH (Big-Bench Hard) is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: It is a curated subset of challenging tasks emphasizing reasoning beyond simple pattern recognition
questions.choice_B: It is exclusively a math competition dataset with difficulty tags
questions.choice_C: It only contains code generation tasks with strict unit tests
questions.choice_D: It is a monolithic benchmark with a single score for reading comprehension only

questions.question: Which best characterizes HumanEval?
questions.choice_A: A multilingual QA benchmark focused on encyclopedic knowledge
questions.choice_B: A Python code generation benchmark with function docstrings and hidden unit tests to evaluate Pass@K
questions.choice_C: A dataset of formal theorems in Isabelle/HOL requiring machine-checked proofs
questions.choice_D: A physics reasoning test with free-form numeric answers

questions.question: How does MBPP differ from HumanEval in typical usage?
questions.choice_A: MBPP consists of image classification tasks while HumanEval is NLP-focused
questions.choice_B: MBPP provides standardized compiler outputs rather than unit tests
questions.choice_C: MBPP contains many simpler Python problems aimed at introductory-level tasks, often with multiple reference tests
questions.choice_D: MBPP uses human grading without automated test cases

questions.question: What is a defining feature of miniF2F in the context of formal mathematics evaluation?
questions.choice_A: It evaluates multi-modal math reasoning with images and audio
questions.choice_B: It focuses on translating informal competition-style problems into formal proofs to test generalization of theorem provers
questions.choice_C: It is a benchmark solely for code optimization in compilers
questions.choice_D: It uses only multiple-choice format to assess proof strategies

questions.question: Which metric is most commonly used for short-answer math benchmarks like GSM8K and MATH?
questions.choice_A: BLEU score
questions.choice_B: Exact-match accuracy after normalization of numeric/string outputs
questions.choice_C: ROUGE-L
questions.choice_D: Character error rate

questions.question: What does Pass@K measure in code generation benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: The percentage of problems solved when selecting the single highest-likelihood sample
questions.choice_B: The average number of lines of code executed per test
questions.choice_C: The probability that at least one of K independently sampled programs passes all unit tests
questions.choice_D: The F1 score of token-level predictions over generated code

questions.question: When would F1 be more appropriate than exact-match for evaluation?
questions.choice_A: For code synthesis tasks with hidden unit tests
questions.choice_B: For multiple-choice exams with four options
questions.choice_C: For span-based QA or multi-token outputs where partial overlap should be credited
questions.choice_D: For numeric answers where whitespace varies

questions.question: Which best describes the difference between zero-shot and few-shot evaluation protocols?
questions.choice_A: Zero-shot allows access to training labels; few-shot prohibits any labels
questions.choice_B: Zero-shot uses no in-context examples; few-shot provides several labeled exemplars in the prompt
questions.choice_C: Zero-shot requires chain-of-thought; few-shot forbids chain-of-thought
questions.choice_D: Zero-shot is only for code; few-shot is only for math

questions.question: What is the motivation behind chain-of-thought prompting in mathematical reasoning benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: To reduce the number of tokens generated by truncating explanations
questions.choice_B: To encourage explicit intermediate reasoning steps that can improve final answer accuracy
questions.choice_C: To avoid the need for any final answer at all
questions.choice_D: To ensure compatibility with multiple-choice evaluation only

questions.question: In self-consistency (majority voting) evaluation, what is the typical procedure?
questions.choice_A: Run a single deterministic decode and trust the first chain-of-thought
questions.choice_B: Sample multiple independent reasoning paths and select the most frequent final answer
questions.choice_C: Use beam search and average token probabilities across beams
questions.choice_D: Ask a human to adjudicate among multiple model outputs

questions.question: How do sample budgets interact with self-consistency evaluation?
questions.choice_A: Larger budgets generally increase the chance of finding a correct answer but also raise compute cost
questions.choice_B: Budgets only matter for multiple-choice tasks
questions.choice_C: Smaller budgets always outperform larger ones due to reduced variance
questions.choice_D: Budgets control the size of the training set rather than the number of samples per question

questions.question: What is a common pitfall when reporting Pass@K on HumanEval?
questions.choice_A: Using exact-match on docstrings rather than unit test outcomes
questions.choice_B: Counting partially passed test suites as full passes
questions.choice_C: Sampling with temperature 0 and claiming Pass@K significantly differs from Pass@1
questions.choice_D: Reporting per-task F1 instead of accuracy

questions.question: Why is prompt contamination a concern in few-shot chain-of-thought evaluations?
questions.choice_A: It prevents models from producing any intermediate steps
questions.choice_B: It can leak target-specific cues or solutions via exemplars, inflating apparent generalization
questions.choice_C: It forces models to answer in multiple-choice format
questions.choice_D: It breaks unit tests by changing function signatures

questions.question: Which statement about evaluation on MMLU versus BBH is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Both are strictly math-only benchmarks
questions.choice_B: MMLU is standardized multiple-choice across many subjects; BBH is a curated set of harder reasoning tasks with varied formats
questions.choice_C: MMLU uses unit tests; BBH uses exact-match numeric answers
questions.choice_D: BBH is easier and mainly for undergraduate general knowledge

questions.question: What is Maj@K intended to capture when reporting results on reasoning benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: The proportion of problems solved by the single best sample
questions.choice_B: The fraction of items for which the majority among K samples yields the correct final answer
questions.choice_C: The average number of reasoning steps per sample
questions.choice_D: The maximum likelihood among K sampled answers

questions.question: When comparing results across GSM8K, MATH, and CMATH, which practice best supports fair conclusions?
questions.choice_A: Use the same decoding hyperparameters, prompt formats, and answer normalization; report both single-sample and self-consistency metrics
questions.choice_B: Change prompts per dataset to maximize accuracy; report only the best number
questions.choice_C: Use temperature 0 for math and temperature 1 for knowledge tasks to standardize
questions.choice_D: Report micro-averaged BLEU over all three datasets
